clue.text: Left on sun hat, about to get hot

indicators.note: in a down-the-page or added-on sense, the left marker is attached on after the hat and about

parts.note: a topi is a lightweight pith helmet worn against the sun
CA is circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Someone puts on a sun hat to the left just before the weather turns hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places the left marker after the hat and 'about'; 'to get' just links wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot news is current and newsworthy, the same idea as a subject that is in the news right now.

clue.text: Maker of 3 also holds display of watches

indicators.note: the word for also wraps around the display

parts.note: too means also
an LED, light-emitting diode, display is used on digital watches

explanation.surface: A watchmaker who also keeps a window display of watches.
explanation.walkthrough: 3 refers to 3-down, cold steel: the Spanish city has been famous for sword blades for centuries.
explanation.definitionFit: Toledo in Spain was renowned for making fine swords, the classic blade weapons.

clue.text: Supplement, perhaps, to leave by train?

definitions.meaning: a detachable section of a newspaper or magazine
a train is said to ... when it departs the station

explanation.definitionFit: A pull-out is a removable magazine section, and to pull out is what a departing train does.

clue.text: Being unemotional, it's appropriate to say something offensively sharp

parts.note: cold means unemotional

indicators.note: the word for appropriate is pronounced, giving a word that is spelt differently but sounds the same

parts.note: to appropriate is to steal

explanation.surface: Someone unemotional finds it fitting to make a cutting remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriate' looks like an adjective (fitting) but is the verb, take for oneself; 'it's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Cold steel means bladed weapons such as swords or bayonets, sharp instruments used offensively.

clue.text: Stuff heatedly hurled out, as politician's left little room

indicators.note: the politician has left, so those letters go out of the room word

parts.note: a lavatory is a small room, the smallest room in the house
a Tory is a British Conservative politician

explanation.surface: A heated speech is thrown at a politician as they leave a small room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link; the 's on politician's means 'has'. A Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Molten rock is ejected hot from a volcano, which is what this material is.

clue.text: House contains an orchid

indicators.note: the house word holds the next word within it

parts.note: a villa is a type of house
taken as written

explanation.surface: A house is home to a single orchid.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanilla is a climbing orchid whose pods give the flavouring.

clue.text: Royal Court Shakespeare production containing wonderful lines

indicators.note: the poetry word holds the other pieces within it

parts.note: Shakespeare produced verses, lines of poetry
A1, written AI, means first-rate
L is the abbreviation for line, so LL is lines

explanation.surface: A Royal Court theatre staging of Shakespeare full of marvellous lines.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the Royal Court Theatre in London; the definition is the French royal court. A1, first-class, is written AI.
explanation.definitionFit: Versailles was the palace and seat of the French royal court under Louis XIV.

clue.text: Gently push new topping off sweet

indicators.note: the top letter is taken off the sweet

parts.note: fudge is a sweet

explanation.surface: Carefully nudge a new decoration off the dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topping off' removes the F from FUDGE, leaving UDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To nudge is to prod someone or something lightly.

clue.text: Complaint — 24 has dispatched header into wrong goal

indicators.note: the trimmed word goes inside the rearranged goal
the letters of goal are wrong, so rearranged
the first letter is sent off

parts.note: the answer to 24-down, dumb

explanation.surface: A football grumble: the player sent his header into his own goal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumbago is lower back pain, an ailment or physical complaint.

clue.text: Scandalised as a Scandinavian turned up and took charge

indicators.note: in a down entry the word is read upwards, so reversed

parts.note: a Lapp is a person from Lapland in northern Scandinavia
led means took charge

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian appeared and took over, to everyone's outrage.
explanation.definitionFit: Appalled means shocked and outraged, the same feeling as being scandalised.

clue.text: Cowardly girl to cohabit with revolutionary

parts.note: Lily is a girl's name
to live with someone is to cohabit
a Red is a communist revolutionary

explanation.surface: A timid girl moves in with a radical boyfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: Lily-livered is an old idiom for timid, from the belief that a pale liver showed a lack of courage.

clue.text: Hair, unkempt but clean

definitions.meaning: an untidy shock of hair is called a ...
to ... is to clean a floor with a ...

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a tousled head of hair and the verb for wiping a floor clean.

clue.text: Ready to drop off weapon -for returning to armoury at last

indicators.note: the weapon word goes back the way it came, read right to left

parts.note: a sword is a weapon

indicators.note: only the final letter of armoury is used

explanation.surface: A weapon going back to the armoury, its owner ready to drop off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns SWORD into DROWS; 'for' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone drowsy is sleepy, about to nod off, which is what 'drop off' means.

clue.text: All Babe's played?

indicators.note: the letters are played around with, rearranged into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the letters of Babe's, S included, go into the mix

explanation.surface: The question of which game Babe Ruth played, the whole of his career.
explanation.walkthrough: Babe Ruth was the great American baseball star, so the whole clue also defines the answer; the anagram of ALL BABES gives it.
explanation.definitionFit: Babe Ruth played baseball throughout his career, so the clue read whole describes the game.

clue.text: Missing out university, anyone could turn into a popular author

indicators.note: the letters turn into a new arrangement once the university letter is taken out

parts.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Anyone could become a bestselling writer without going to university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missing out' removes U from ANYONE COULD before 'turn into' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Conan Doyle, creator of Sherlock Holmes, was a hugely popular author.

clue.text: A United Nations programme?

parts.note: a planet united as one would be a fitting description of the UN, but this is a BBC Radio 4 lunchtime news programme

explanation.definitionFit: It is the long-running BBC Radio 4 news programme at one o'clock, read whimsically as the globe united.

clue.text: Settling area and starting fire

parts.note: lighting a fire is starting it

explanation.surface: Settling down in an area and starting a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird alighting on a branch is settling there after flight.

clue.text: Suppress strong feelings, seeing son deteriorate

parts.note: to moulder is to rot or decay

explanation.surface: Bottling up emotion while watching one's son go downhill.
explanation.definitionFit: To smoulder is to burn with suppressed emotion such as anger or desire.

clue.text: Yanks that are fairly well off in Mexico, for example

definitions.text: Yanks that are fairly well off
definitions.meaning: the comfortable mainstream middle class of the USA
Mexico is in the central part of the Americas

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the US heartland middle class and, literally, the central part of the Americas, which includes Mexico.

clue.text: Sort of publishing, that often supports a mass of papers?

definitions.meaning: producing printed matter with a personal computer

definitions.text: that often supports a mass of papers?
definitions.meaning: the surface of a desk, piled high with documents

explanation.definitionFit: Desktop publishing is a kind of page design on a PC, and a literal desk top bears heaps of paperwork.

clue.text: Bimbo has a passion, notice, to catch husband

indicators.note: the passion word catches the husband letter inside it

parts.note: ire is passionate anger
an ad is a notice

explanation.surface: A bimbo has a crush and puts up a notice to land a husband.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal and dismissive for an empty-headed person.

clue.text: Odd grouping in exercise held -by chief

indicators.note: the exercise letters are held inside the chief word

parts.note: a head is a chief
PT is physical training, exercise

explanation.surface: An odd group gathered in an exercise class led by the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link. Seven is an odd number, hence 'odd grouping'.
explanation.definitionFit: A heptad is a group of seven, and seven is an odd number.

clue.text: Not even the occasional girlfriend?

definitions.meaning: someone who is not a regular partner is literally not a steady

explanation.definitionFit: Unsteady means wobbly; whimsically it is a date who is not your steady.

clue.text: Cut up writing papers

indicators.note: in a down entry the word is read upwards, so reversed

parts.note: to axe is to cut
MS, manuscript, is a piece of writing

explanation.surface: Cutting up sheets of writing paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writing papers' looks like one phrase but splits: 'writing' is wordplay and 'papers' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: School or university tests are commonly called papers.

clue.text: Accusation in Lord Cardigan's order to his brigade

definitions.text: Lord Cardigan's order to his brigade
definitions.meaning: Cardigan led the Light Brigade in its famous attack at Balaclava in 1854

explanation.definitionFit: A criminal accusation is a charge, and the order to attack given to the Light Brigade was the cavalry command of the same word.

clue.text: Struck with amazement to see elephant with 'tail docked

indicators.note: the last letter is cut off, like a docked tail

parts.note: Dumbo is the Disney cartoon elephant

explanation.surface: Astonished at the sight of an elephant whose tail has been cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: To be struck dumb is to be speechless with astonishment.

clue.text: I should have this for completeness in another case

definitions.text: I should have this for completeness in another case

parts.words: I should have this for completeness in another case
parts.note: the capital letter I needs nothing more, but the lower-case form is incomplete without the small mark above it

explanation.definitionFit: A small lower-case i carries a little mark over it, which a capital lacks, so it needs this mark to be complete.

clue.text: It's' often staged because it's popular

definitions.text: It's' often staged because it's popular

parts.words: It's' often staged because it's popular
parts.note: a Shakespeare comedy frequently performed, its title also meaning that the audience enjoys it

explanation.definitionFit: This is Shakespeare's comedy of the Forest of Arden, a frequently performed play whose title also suggests audience approval.

clue.text: Old priest's shaky response

indicators.note: the letters are unsteady and shaken up into a new order

parts.note: the letters of priest

explanation.surface: An elderly cleric gives a hesitant reply.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick retort, a sharp reply.

clue.text: City father's case first to be heard

parts.note: a bag is a case for carrying things

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: dad is a word for father

explanation.surface: A city's father has his court case heard first.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of father's just links DAD to the case; 'first to be heard' gives H.
explanation.definitionFit: Baghdad is the capital city of Iraq.
